heard: You cannot see the most common star in the sky. These dim embers make up 80% of our galaxy. Even our closest neighbor, Proxima Centauri, is hidden in the dark. These are red dwarfs, small stars that act like cosmic marathon runners. While our sun is a rare giant, these stars burn for trillions of years. In fact, not a single one has ever died yet. The universe is simply too young for them to burn out. They are the ultimate survivors you will never see.
